text:
oncall-bot: P1 alert — High latency detected for enterprise tenant ACME-PROD on dedicated pool eu-west-1. p95 ~ 2.4s (normal 100ms), p99 spike > 30s, error rate elevated. Paging maria-ops (primary oncall) and jake-sre. Incident channel: #incidents — please acknowledge.

maria-ops: ack. I’m on it. creating war room and adding customer personnel. @anna-cs please standby for a customer update.

jake-sre: ack. joining. first glance — traffic concentrated on dedicated pool rdp-eu-west-1-ded-03 for ACME-PROD, queue depth high, GPU utilization uneven across nodes.

li-runtime: jumping in. recent deploy? rolling restarts? checking model kernel logs and runtime OOMs.

sre-runbook-bot: Recommended runbook: "Dedicated pool latency > p99" — step 1 check queue and KV cache hit rates; step 2 isolate tenant traffic; step 3 failover to warm spare pool; step 4 scale pool. Run commands listed.

maria-ops: checked deployments — no recent user-triggered deploys for ACME-PROD in the last 3 hours. No config rollouts.

jake-sre: I can see a pattern — a subset of hosts showing repeated long tail token generation stalls. Dumping tail logs now:
```
[runtime] 2025-11-12T09:12:34Z host=rde-03 - kvcache.miss=0.03 kernel=matmul_quant float32->int8 fallback latency=29.6s
[runtime] 2025-11-12T09:12:35Z host=rde-03 - inflight.requests=124 queue.len=48
```
Seems like KV cache pressure + a quantized kernel fallback on one node.

li-runtime: if a kernel fallback is hitting float path on certain nodes that could explain p99. Are those nodes using older CUDA or driver mismatch? Checking node labels…

ops-lead: tagging infra team, possible transient NV driver/firmware mismatch after maintenance window earlier. @infra-sig-team please advise.

anna-cs: ACME-PROD is in a business-critical window, they're noticing degraded UX. I'll draft customer-safe message once we have mitigation plan.

maria-ops: Mitigation options: 1) isolate ACME traffic to healthy nodes in the eu-west-1 fleet (tenant isolation), 2) shift ACME to warm spare dedicated pool in another region eu-central-1 as temporary fallback, 3) scale up dedicated pool by adding 4 spare GPUs, 4) apply targeted config to force kernel choice (if safe). Preference for fast mitigation: #1 + #2. Thoughts?

jake-sre: #1 isolate tenant is lowest risk and fastest if we can reprogram routing quickly. I'll take routing. li-runtime take kernel checks and blocklist the problematic host. maria-ops can you coordinate with ops to cordon rde-03?

li-runtime: running diagnostics on rde-03: driver 525.85, others at 525.89. There is a small diff. Also found repeated CUDA memalloc failures in logs preceding stalls. Possible flaky NIC causing retransmits and KV cache misses.

jake-sre: starting routing change: updating policy to pin ACME-PROD to pool eu-west-1-ded-{01,02,04} and set rde-03 to drain. Command: `redwoodctl routes update --tenant acme-prod --pool eu-west-1-ded --exclude rde-03`

sre-runbook-bot: Action logged. Please monitor p95/p99 after routing change.

maria-ops: executing cordon/drain on rde-03 now. `infractl host cordon rde-03 && infractl host drain rde-03 --grace 30s`

(reacts: jake-sre :thumbsup:)

maria-ops: routing change applied. telemetry shows immediate drop in queue depth for rde-03. Observability: p95 dropped to 180ms, p99 down to 3.2s — still above SLO but much improved.

anna-cs: sending customer note: "We're investigating elevated latency in your dedicated pool in eu-west-1. We've moved your traffic away from affected hosts and are closely monitoring. Expect updates in 15 min." Sending now.

jake-sre: good. I'll keep rde-03 drained and run GPU memtests and driver reconcile. If hardware flaky, we should reprovision.

li-runtime: continuing kernel investigation. Found a model-specific quantization path that on rare inputs triggers long compile on that node — combined with memalloc failures it caused fallback. I've pushed a safe server-side patch to prefer precompiled kernels for that model for ACME tenants. Patch id: patch-20251112-qa1. Rolling canary now to {01,02}.

maria-ops: can we avoid rolling on the whole pool until hardware check done? prefer targeted config.

li-runtime: yes canary only targeted for ACME tenant traffic. No global rollout.

ops-lead: infra ran memtest — rde-03 shows ECC errors and NIC CRC warnings. Plan: reprovision host, replace GPU and NIC. ETA 45m. We'll keep it drained.

jake-sre: since rde-03 is a hot node for ACME, confirm capacity headroom in the rest of the pool. If pressure continues, we may need to burst to eu-central-1 warm spare.

maria-ops: current capacity headroom ~12% but requests per second for ACME trending down after routing. set autoscale buffer to +20% for this pool as precaution. `redwoodctl pool scale eu-west-1-ded --buffer 20%`

sre-runbook-bot: Scale action recorded. Expected convergence 3m.

maria-ops: monitoring: after scale and routing, p95=120ms, p99=600ms. Error rate normalized. Customer UX should be much better.

anna-cs: updated ACME: "We've routed your traffic away from affected hosts and applied a temporary mitigation. We're replacing hardware and will follow up when fully resolved. Please ping me if you still see degradation."

jake-sre: documenting post-incident items: 1) add driver/firmware drift detection on dedicate pools; 2) improve per-node kernel fallback metrics; 3) stronger KV cache eviction insights per-tenant; 4) playbook step to prefer tenant-level kernel pinning as quick mitigation.

li-runtime: agree. also schedule a test to reproduce quantization compile corner-case with ACME model.

maria-ops: current status: mitigation in place, customer notified, hardware replacement underway, monitoring p99 for 1h. I'll handoff to night oncall at 1752006000 with notes.

ops-lead: confirm handoff procedure: create incident summary, attach logs, add runbook steps and actions taken.

maria-ops: summary prepared and pinned in this thread. everyone please add any missing notes.

anna-cs: ACME responded: "Thanks for the fast response — latency back to normal now. Please keep us posted on root cause and replacement timeline."

jake-sre: thanks team. keeping this thread open for postmortem. I'll add the technical timeline and RCA draft tomorrow.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled handoff at 1752006000 to night oncall.

maria-ops: closing war room for active mitigation. marking as MONITORING. reopen if we see regressions.

(reacts: anna-cs :white_check_mark:)
